industry.summary: Indian private hospitals are in a bed-building cycle financed by strong cash flows, while price (ARPOB) rather than volume has driven growth for the established chains. Narayana is the outlier on cost: its existing India beds cost ~₹75 lakh each (gross block + CWIP ÷ operational beds), but new beds now cost ₹1.8-2.6 cr (construction costs are ~60% higher than five years ago, per management). Abroad it owns a US-dollar hospital business in the Cayman Islands and, since Nov-2025, an NHS-funded UK hospital group.
themes: NH's six projects cost ₹1.8-2.6 cr per owned bed (HSR ₹2.3 cr, Rajarhat ₹2.6 cr, South Bengaluru ₹2.3 cr, Raipur ₹1.8 cr; leased Central Bengaluru ₹0.7 cr) vs ~₹0.75 cr for today's network; management: construction costs +60% in five years. Peers are adding beds in NH's cities (an analyst on the Q1 call: 'every other hospital is adding beds').

NH India ARPOB +13% in FY26 and +9% in Q1FY27 on case mix (robotic cardiac ~100 a month, ~160 TAVIs a year at Bengaluru), shorter stays and payer mix; list-price rises are only low-to-mid single digit. Occupied beds fell ~5% over FY24-26 and recovered in Q1FY27 (IP +8%).
Payer mix: insurance up, schemes slow to pay
Q1FY27 India hospital revenue: walk-in 43%, insured 33%, government schemes 18% (CGHS, ESIS, state schemes: lower tariffs; AR FY26 notes delayed collections from government payers), international 5%.
India's international patient revenue fell 9% in FY26 (₹216 cr) as NH stopped active marketing amid uncertainty (Bangladesh), then rose 58% YoY in Q1FY27 off a low base.

NH says it runs India's only hospital-promoted health insurer; start-ups are trying similar prepaid models (Q4FY26 call). Combined clinic and insurance losses were ₹139 cr in FY26 across India and Cayman.

NHS waiting list 7.4 mn (Aug-2025) vs 4.6 mn pre-Covid, 2.9 mn waiting over 18 weeks; NHS outsourcing to independents £18 bn (FY24, 6% CAGR); private outpatient and day-care market ~£15 bn (CY2025E). PPG is ~95% NHS-funded vs ~35% at Spire and 60-70% at Ramsay (management).

~45% of FY27E revenue is earned in US$ and GBP. The rupee averaged ~₹88.3/US$ in FY26 and ~₹94.7 in Q1FY27 (deck and PL rupee figures), which lifts reported Cayman and UK numbers; debt includes US$115 mn and £150 mn, serviced from those businesses' own cash flow.

critiques: The India hospital volume engine stalled: occupied beds fell from ~2,774 (FY24) to ~2,648 (FY26) and growth came from ARPOB; no new beds since listing until FY27
GAM reading of company KPIs; management (Q4FY26 call)
New beds cost ₹1.8-2.6 cr each against ~₹0.75 cr for the existing network, and three of six projects slipped a year in the Aug-2026 deck
q1ppt vs q4ppt; analysts on the Q4FY26 call
Two insurers and a clinic chain lost ₹139 cr in FY26 and ~₹68 cr in Q1FY27 alone; India's claims ratio was 219%
The UK deal bought a 95%-NHS, ~9% margin business with £150 mn of acquisition debt; Q1FY27 margins fell on a heatwave and software certification is 4-6 months late
Cayman growth is slowing (hospital +5% in Q1FY27) and is one island: a hurricane, regulatory change or a competitor would hit over a third of group EBITDA
Founder pay of ₹23.8 cr in FY26 is high for a hospital chain this size, and related-party purchases from a KMP-linked supplier doubled to ₹17 cr
Segment profit is opaque: the company does not report Cayman EBITDA ('work it out') and the India figure includes income eliminated on consolidation
gaps: Occupancy is not disclosed (management: 'typically 60-65%' on an undisclosed bed base); our occupied-bed figures are India hospital revenue ÷ ARPOB.

Cayman hospital EBITDA is not disclosed; we use PL's split (Cayman FY26 ₹694 cr, 45.6%), which moves ~₹79 cr from the company's India hospital EBITDA to Cayman. On the company's own India figure Cayman's margin is ~39%.
The FY26 split of the ₹67 cr NHIC + NHIL loss between clinics and insurance is not disclosed (Q1FY27: clinics ~₹15 cr, NHIL PAT ₹-20.1 cr).
NHIL's FY26 revenue is derived (AR insurance segment ₹385.65 cr less CIHL ₹368.9 cr = ~₹16.8 cr).
No UK capex plan (management: 'too early'); no Cayman expansion capex. Our capex includes ~₹80-100 cr a year of overseas maintenance as a GAM estimate.
FX: forecasts use the Q1FY27 average rates implied by company and PL figures (₹94.7/US$, ₹127/£); we did not source a 30-Sep-2026 spot rate.

Broker methods: ICICI Direct's 29-Jun-2026 note (method assumed as in its 27-May note), Kotak's full SOTP (only a summary: ~17x pre-Ind AS for India), HSBC's method, and Geojit's and BP Wealth's methods were not available to us.
Institutional holders' individual stakes at Jun-2026 were not found (names only from the deck).
Cluster or hospital-level EBITDA, mature vs new hospitals, and capex per project spent to date are not disclosed.
Lease payments for FY27-29E are not guided; for the pre-Ind AS translation we use contractual rent due within one year (₹162 cr, AR FY26 note 18) and grow it with new leases.
conflicts: India hospital EBITDA FY26: company ₹1,095 cr (23.1%) vs PL ₹1,016 cr; quarterly gaps are uneven (Q2FY26 company ₹290 cr vs PL ₹243 cr; Q3FY26 ₹263 cr vs ₹270 cr). We model on PL's split because it sums to consolidated EBITDA, and show the company figure as the KPI.
Clinic revenue FY25: company ₹40.7 cr (AR FY26: FY26 ₹60.9 cr, +49.8%) vs PL ₹32.9 cr; we use the company figure.
Screener's FY26 EBITDA (₹1,641 cr) is ~₹24 cr above the company's ex-other-income figure after the one-time cost (₹1,617 cr) and its interest ₹22 cr higher; the quarters agree.
Kotak's '~17x FY28E pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA' may be the multiple the price implies rather than its target multiple; the summary is ambiguous.
PPG EBITDA: the Oct-2025 deck's £20 mn FY25 adjusted EBITDA was pre-IFRS 16; post-IFRS 16 it was £29 mn (Nov-2025 call); both exclude £6.1 mn of Birmingham start-up losses.
